text:
Claude Giroux played 1,000 games for the Flyers, and at 38 he is still finding ways to make headlines in Ottawa. He scored against his old team this month, reunited with the Boucher family when Tyler Boucher, son of his former Philadelphia teammate Brian, joined him in Ottawa, and one Hall of Famer went on record saying Giroux belongs in the Hall himself. He had 1,165 career points before this season.

He's still useful in ways the box score undersells. At five on five the Senators take 60% of the expected goals with him on the ice, 6.8 points better than without him, one of the best marks on the team. His points (13 in 25) have been held down because Ottawa has scored 5.3 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him out there, and that usually swings back. Evolving-Hockey had him 47th among forwards in wins above replacement last season, which is remarkable at his age. Our range projects 38 to 56 points. Expect the assists to pick up.
